name: Mog battle threads

card.summary: A forum thread format in which two faces are posted side by side and members vote on who looks better, giving users an outside comparison of their own looks.
card.note: Results are crowd opinion from anonymous forum members, and replies can be blunt.

quick.overview:
A mog battle thread puts two photos next to each other, such as two users, friends, or celebrities, and asks the forum which face "mogs" (looks better than) the other. Members reply with a pick and often a short reason.

For someone working on their appearance, the thread works as a quick outside comparison. Replies usually point to specific features, such as eye area, jaw, skin or hair, that members think decided the matchup, which some users treat as a list of things to improve. No research has examined these threads; they are a community custom.
quick.how: A poster uploads two images, sometimes labeled A and B, and titles the thread "mog battle" with optional names. Others vote in replies or with a poll and explain their choice. Some threads pit a member's current photos against an earlier photo of themselves, or compare two forum regulars. Threads typically fill within hours to days.
quick.risks: Replies come from anonymous users, can be harsh, and reflect the forum's own taste rather than any measured standard. Posting personal photos to a public forum carries privacy considerations, including that images can be saved and re-shared. Users who are sensitive to criticism may find the feedback distressing.

lead: Mog battle threads are a recurring post format on looksmaxxing forums in which two faces are placed side by side and the community votes on which one "mogs", meaning looks better than, the other.[1][2] The term "mogging" refers to asserting dominance over another person through appearance, and is one of the core vocabulary words of the looksmaxxing community.[3]

Members use the format to see how a face compares with another in the eyes of peers. Replies often name the features they think decided the result, such as the eye area, jawline, or skin, which readers can use as pointers for what to improve.[4][5] Titles on looksmax.org include battles between two users, between a user and a friend, between forum regulars, and between celebrities.[2][5][6] No academic research has studied the format itself.

chain: Post two faces side by side
Community votes and names deciding features
User learns what peers notice and may work on it
angle.text: The thread gives a quick crowd comparison of one face against another. The comments that explain a vote can point toward specific features, such as skin, hair or the eye area, that a person may then choose to work on.

paras: A mog battle begins with an original poster uploading two images and asking which person mogs the other. Many threads carry only the title and the images; others add a prompt such as asking for a verdict from the forum's more experienced raters.[1][2] Replies are short, often a single word naming the winner, and sometimes a line on why.

Matchups vary. Some compare two members, some compare a member to a celebrity or to an earlier photo of themselves, and some compare two friends of the poster.[5][6] Thread titles on looksmax.org show the range, including battles among well-known forum members and a battle between two eye colors.[5][7]

The vocabulary comes from the PSL-forum era of looksmaxxing, whose forums rated men's faces on a numeric scale and gave rise to terms such as mogging.[3] Mog battle threads continue that habit of ranking faces against each other and are posted regularly on looksmax.org, with many threads under near-identical titles.[1][8]

Commenters frequently justify a vote by pointing to features such as bone structure, facial proportions or skin quality, using forum terms that vary between users.[4] Members who post their own photos report using the replies as a gauge of how they are perceived; the wiki's other entries on facial features describe the measures forum members commonly cite.

Responses on forum threads can be blunt, and votes come from a small, self-selected group of users whose standards are specific to the community. Posting identifiable photos online also carries ordinary privacy considerations.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, mog battle threads are a common way to settle who looks better and to ask the forum for a verdict.[1][5]

claims.claim: A side-by-side vote shows which face is objectively better looking
claims.believers: Participants treat the majority vote and the explanations as a ranking of the two faces.[1][4]
claims.experts: No published studies have examined forum voting threads. Research on facial attractiveness generally measures ratings from larger and more varied panels than a forum audience.

claims.claim: The comments reveal which specific features to improve
claims.believers: Users say replies naming the eye area, jaw or skin tell them what to prioritize.[4]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested whether forum feedback leads to appearance changes people value.
